rundown: Tigers beat Bulls 52-41 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, FL. Tigers led 28-17 at the half and never looked back. The 1st quarter decided it: Tigers won it 21-0.
Scoring: Tigers 7 touchdowns and 1 field goal; Bulls 5 touchdowns and 2 field goals. The last score: J. Carter run for 26 yds, for a TD (P. Laforge KICK) (4th quarter, 0:44).

Leading the way — Tigers: Marcus Stokes 15/31, 313 yds, 3 TD; Jaylin Carter 21 car, 109 yds, 2 TD; Jemyri Davis 5 rec, 161 yds, 1 TD. Bulls: Luke Kromenhoek 22/37, 271 yds, 3 TD, 30 car, 146 yds, 1 TD; Mudia Reuben 6 rec, 98 yds, 2 TD.
Where Tigers won it: they outgained them 581 yards to 552 and won the turnover battle (0 to 1).
Against the closing line (DraftKings): Tigers closed as 4.5-point favorites and covered by 6.5; the total closed at 51.5 and they combined for 93, over by 41.5.

review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 12, 7:58 PM ET. It had Tigers 67% and Bulls 33%, projecting Tigers 30.4 – Bulls 23.9 (54.3 total, Tigers by 6.5).

Final: Tigers 52 – Bulls 41. Right winner: it had Tigers at 67%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Tigers came in with a 7% above average attack and a 5% stingier than average defense (7-2, 37.6 scored and 23.6 allowed a game over 9 games), worth about 163 and 163 games of evidence. Projected to score 30.4, they scored 52 (+21.6 points, 71% over); projected to allow 23.9, they allowed 41 (+17.1 points, 72% over).

Bulls came in with a 6% below average attack and a league-average defense (6-3, 25.9 scored and 15.1 allowed a game over 9 games), worth about 172 and 172 games of evidence. Projected to score 23.9, they scored 41 (+17.1 points, 72% over); projected to allow 30.4, they allowed 52 (+21.6 points, 71% over).

The bigger miss was Tigers' scoring (+21.6 points against projection); both sides outscored their projections, so the game ran hotter than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 93 against 54.3 projected (+38.7), about the 99th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±15.5).

Margin: Tigers by 11 against Tigers by 6.5 projected, about the 38th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±15.3).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.body:
Splits (Action Network): spread: 65% of bets on Tigers, 51% of the money — Tigers covered; total: 73% of bets on the over, 88% of the money — it went over; moneyline: 90% of bets on Tigers, 57% of the money.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.643 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -6 points. It counts toward CFB scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 68 graded CFB games the algo now scales scoring ×0.967 and gives home teams -1.5 points. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total outside its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
